samples.summary: Divider drag has no `pointercancel` handler — now reachable via touch, it leaves window listeners and global body styles stuck
samples.evidence: `onDividerPointerDown` registers `window.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove)` / `('pointerup', onUp)` and sets `document.body.style.cursor`/`userSelect`, but nothing listens for `pointercancel`. This change adds `divider.style.touchAction = 'none'` (line 294) specifically to make touch dragging work, and touch is exactly the input where the browser fires `pointercancel` instead of `pointerup` (e.g. a second finger arriving, or the gesture being taken over). When that happens `onUp` never runs: `endDrag` stays set, `user-select: none` and `cursor: col-resize` stay applied to `document.body` app-wide, and the still-attached `pointermove` listener keeps resizing the panes on every subsequent pointer move with no button/finger down until the next unrelated pointerup. Contained (any later click clears it), but it is a real stuck-state/listener leak on the path this diff newly enables.
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts drag handler (lines 486-521) and dispose (635-642)

samples.summary: Divider drag ignores the grab offset inside the now-25px hit area, so the hairline jumps up to 12px on grab — contradicting the comment that claims exact tracking
samples.evidence: `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track` places the left pane's width at exactly `clientX - rect.left`, i.e. the divider's LEFT EDGE is put under the pointer regardless of where inside the 25px band the drag started. With the old 7px band the worst-case jump was ~7px; at 25px (padding `0 12px`) a user who grabs the visible 1px hairline (the band's centre) sees the hairline snap ~12px left on pointerdown and stay 12px offset for the whole drag. The added comment asserts the new formula makes the pane width `ratio * track` "exactly" and removes the trailing — it fixes the width-vs-track scaling error but not the grab offset, which is now the larger of the two errors. Fix is to capture `e.clientX - divider.getBoundingClientRect().left` at pointerdown and subtract it.

samples.summary: Share-link image upload failures are reported to nobody: the new `uploadImage` has no error handling, unlike the workspace route's
samples.evidence: `uploadImage = shareTokenImageUploader(token)` is handed straight to `NotesView`. `shareTokenImageUploader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40) REJECTS on any failure (unsupported type, oversize, 403 for a revoked/expired token, network error). The notes engine swallows that rejection: `beginUpload` catches it with `failed()` which only does `console.error` and returns `null`, and the commit step then just removes the placeholder (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-203). So an editor-role visitor whose upload fails sees the placeholder silently vanish with no explanation. The workspace route deliberately wraps the uploader to toast the failure (`handleUploadImage`, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:208-231); this layout, which claims to be "the state ... the workspace route's", drops that error path.
